name: fenics-showcase
title: FEniCS showcase: FEM solvers as composable pbg processes
description:
Seven studies build up from validation to composition to advanced,
showcase-tier physics. `poisson-validation` and `mesh-convergence`
establish that the dolfinx bridge reproduces textbook FEM numerics
(manufactured-solution correctness, O(h^2) P1 convergence).
`transient-diffusion` extends the bridge to time-stepped Processes and
checks mass conservation under backward-Euler integration.
`reaction-diffusion` is the coupling headline: it wires `DiffusionProcess`
and `LogisticReactionProcess` into the same `stores.solution` /
`stores.source` paths and shows Fisher-KPP-like mass growth emerges from
that wiring alone -- the composability property the core of the
investigation exists to demonstrate. Three ADVANCED studies extend the
showcase beyond scalar diffusion/reaction: `navier-stokes` is the first
fluid-dynamics demo (lid-driven cavity, IPCS operator splitting, coupled
P2/P1 velocity-pressure spaces); `moving-boundary` is the first
deforming-domain demo (prescribed-ALE mesh motion re-solved every
substep); `complex-geometry` is the first non-rectangular-domain demo
(gmsh-constructed obstacle/L-shape/annulus topologies imported into
dolfinx). Runs are authored here (Task 7, extended Task 12); execution
recorded into the workspace's `.pbg/runs.jsonl` run log plus behavior-test
evaluation happens in Task 8.
question:
Can modern FEniCSx be wrapped as composable pbg processes that reproduce
canonical FEM results and enable bigraph coupling?
hypothesis:
Wrapping dolfinx's Poisson, transient-diffusion, and logistic-reaction
solvers as process-bigraph Steps/Processes preserves their numerical
fidelity (manufactured-solution validation, O(h^2) mesh convergence,
mass-conserving time-stepping) AND enables genuine bigraph composition:
Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion dynamics should emerge purely from two
independently-authored processes (DiffusionProcess, LogisticReactionProcess)
sharing bigraph stores, with neither process aware of the other.

executive.what_is_this:
A showcase investigation proving that a real external FEM solver
(FEniCSx/dolfinx, not a mock or reimplementation) can be wrapped as
process-bigraph Steps/Processes and composed like any other pbg model.
Two validation studies (`poisson-validation`, `mesh-convergence`) confirm
numerical fidelity against known analytic/theoretical results; two
dynamics studies (`transient-diffusion`, `reaction-diffusion`) extend the
bridge to time-stepping and cross-process coupling. Three ADVANCED
studies (`navier-stokes`, `moving-boundary`, `complex-geometry`) push
the same bridge into fluid dynamics, deforming domains, and
gmsh-generated non-rectangular geometry.
executive.verdict:
Authored and lint-clean: 7 studies, each with a real `@composite_generator`
baseline, a `sims/run.py` canonical runner, and an interactive viz.
Standalone execution of every runner reproduces the expected numerics:
l2_error ~2.8e-13 (poisson-validation, tol 1e-10), observed convergence
rate ~2.00 (mesh-convergence, P1 -> O(h^2)), mass conserved with a
decaying peak (transient-diffusion), reaction-driven mass growth
~2.6e9x the near-zero-reaction control while the field stays bounded
near K=1.0 (reaction-diffusion), a quasi-steady, approximately
divergence-free lid-driven cavity flow stable across Re=100..1000
(navier-stokes), a deforming-mesh diffusion solve whose boundary tracks
the prescribed law to near machine precision with a domain measure that
scales with amplitude (moving-boundary), and finite, bounded,
non-trivial Poisson solutions on three gmsh-generated topologies
(complex-geometry).
executive.verdict_detail:
Task 7 scope: author the investigation + 4 core studies + runners and
get them lint-clean and individually executable (done). Tasks 9-11
scope: author the 3 advanced studies (navier-stokes, moving-boundary,
complex-geometry) with the same rigor (done). Task 12 scope (this task):
bind all 7 studies into this investigation's `studies:` list and extend
`acceptance_criteria` accordingly (done). Task 8 scope (not yet done):
drive these runners through `/viva-study run-script` so results land in
the workspace's `.pbg/runs.jsonl` run log and the dashboard's Tests tab
reflects the behavior tests declared below.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
A real dolfinx bridge, wrapped as ordinary process-bigraph Steps and
Processes, reproduces canonical FEM validation results (MMS correctness,
O(h^2) P1 convergence, mass-conserving transient diffusion) and, when two
independently-authored processes are wired to the same bigraph stores,
produces genuine Fisher-KPP coupling -- without either process containing
any knowledge of the other. The showcase now spans validation ->
coupling -> fluid dynamics -> moving boundaries -> complex geometry:
the same bridge that passes MMS/convergence checks and demonstrates
store-wiring composability also drives a real incompressible
Navier-Stokes solve, a prescribed-ALE deforming-mesh diffusion solve,
and Poisson solves on gmsh-generated non-rectangular topologies --
without departing from the bridge validated in the first four studies.
evidence_for: poisson-validation: l2_error ~2.8e-13 against a quadratic manufactured solution with degree-2 Lagrange elements (Galerkin-exact), well inside the 1e-10 tolerance.
mesh-convergence: observed P1 convergence rate ~2.00 across resolution=[8,16,32] on a superconvergence-resistant (crossed-diagonal) mesh, matching O(h^2) theory.

transient-diffusion: the gaussian bump's peak decays under backward-Euler diffusion while the FEM-integral mass stays flat (Neumann/no-flux boundary), confirming the time-stepped Process wrapper conserves mass.

reaction-diffusion: mass growth with LogisticReactionProcess coupled in (r=2.0) is orders of magnitude larger than a near-zero-reaction control (r=1e-9, identical wiring) run for the same duration -- the growth is attributable to the composed reaction term, not solver noise -- while the field stays bounded near the logistic carrying capacity K=1.0.

navier-stokes: the lid-driven cavity reaches quasi-steady state (<5% residual change in speed_integral between late checkpoints), the converged velocity field is approximately divergence-free (mean|div(u)| ~0.003-0.02), and the IPCS scheme stays stable (no blow-up) across a Re=[100,400,1000] sweep.

moving-boundary: boundary_position tracks the prescribed oscillation law to near machine precision, the FEM-assembled domain_measure's swing scales with oscillation amplitude across an amplitude sweep, and the diffusion field stays finite/bounded throughout on the deforming mesh.

complex-geometry: all three gmsh-generated topologies (obstacle, L-shape, annulus) import with cell counts in the low thousands (well above the 20-cell floor), and each Poisson solve is finite, bounded, and non-trivially nonzero, matching the maximum-principle expectation.
evidence_against: All seven studies use a single fixed random-free deterministic setup (one resolution/degree/parameter point per study beyond the declared sweeps); broader parameter robustness beyond the declared sweeps (resolution in mesh-convergence, rate in reaction-diffusion, Reynolds in navier-stokes, amplitude/mode in moving-boundary, geometry in complex-geometry) is untested.

Behavior tests are authored (Tasks 7, 9-11) but not yet run through the dashboard's Tests tab against the workspace's `.pbg/runs.jsonl` run log (Task 8), so the PASS/FAIL verdicts above come from the runner scripts' own printed checks, not the dashboard's evaluator.
caveats: The coupling composability claim is demonstrated for one process pair (DiffusionProcess / LogisticReactionProcess); it is not yet exercised against a third, unrelated process to further stress-test the claim that the wiring pattern generalizes.

The three advanced studies (navier-stokes, moving-boundary, complex-geometry) each stand on their own dolfinx bridge exercise -- they are not yet cross-wired into a single combined composite (e.g. fluid flow on a deforming, non-rectangular domain), so the showcase demonstrates breadth of individual capability, not their joint composition.

studies.name: poisson-validation
studies.title: Poisson validation: MMS correctness
studies.question:
Does the dolfinx-backed `PoissonSolverStep` reproduce the exact solution of
a manufactured steady Poisson problem to numerical precision?

studies.name: mesh-convergence
studies.title: Mesh convergence: FEM rigor
studies.question:
Does the `PoissonSolverStep` wrapper deliver the theoretical O(h^2) mesh
convergence rate for P1 Lagrange elements, or does the wrapping introduce
an artifact that masks/inflates the true discretization error?

studies.name: transient-diffusion
studies.title: Transient diffusion: time-stepping
studies.question:
Does a time-stepped `DiffusionProcess` (backward-Euler, dolfinx-backed)
conserve mass under a no-flux boundary while smoothing/decaying an initial
field, when driven through process-bigraph's own Composite tick loop
(not called directly)?

studies.name: reaction-diffusion
studies.title: Reaction-diffusion: bigraph coupling (headline)
studies.question:
Do two independently-authored processes -- `DiffusionProcess` (no
knowledge of reactions) and `LogisticReactionProcess` (no knowledge of
FEM/diffusion) -- produce genuine Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion dynamics
when wired to the same bigraph stores, with neither process calling into
the other?

studies.name: navier-stokes
studies.title: Navier-Stokes: lid-driven cavity flow (IPCS)
studies.question:
Does a real dolfinx incompressible Navier-Stokes solve -- Taylor-Hood-ish
P2/P1 velocity/pressure, classic IPCS (Incremental Pressure Correction
Scheme) operator splitting -- reproduce the textbook lid-driven-cavity
flow (a non-trivial, approximately divergence-free, quasi-steady
recirculating flow pinned near the lid velocity) when wrapped as a
process-bigraph Process, and does the scheme stay numerically stable
across a moderate Reynolds-number sweep?

studies.name: moving-boundary
studies.title: Moving boundary: diffusion on a deforming (ALE) domain
studies.question:
Does a real dolfinx diffusion solve, re-assembled and re-solved every
substep on a mesh whose geometry is mutated in place according to a
prescribed moving-boundary law (prescribed ALE mesh motion), stay
numerically well-behaved -- boundary tracking the prescribed law, domain
measure scaling correctly with the deformation amplitude, field staying
finite -- when wrapped as a process-bigraph Process?

studies.name: complex-geometry
studies.title: Complex geometry: gmsh-generated non-trivial domains
studies.question:
Does a real gmsh-constructed non-trivial planar geometry -- imported into
dolfinx via `dolfinx.io.gmsh.model_to_mesh` -- produce a genuine
unstructured triangulation with a positive cell count, and does a real
Poisson solve on that imported mesh (homogeneous Dirichlet boundary, a
constant interior source) stay finite, bounded, and non-trivially
nonzero, across three qualitatively different domain topologies (a
simply-connected domain with a circular hole, a non-convex re-entrant
corner, and a multiply-connected annulus)?
